---
title: "Why do I feel broke even when the numbers say I'm not?"
pubDate: 2026-07-09
description: "You earn well. You save. You still wake up at 3am running the numbers. Here's what that pattern is actually about."
author: Joel
tags: [money-vigilance, behavioural-money, self-development]
---

You've checked the balance. You know it's fine. You check again anyway.

Not because something went wrong. Because something in you needs to be sure — and sure doesn't seem to stick.

This is one of the most common patterns Joel sees in clients who earn well and still feel financially unsafe. The account is healthy. The dread is not.

Money vigilance isn't a flaw in your character. It's a strategy that worked at some point. Maybe money was genuinely tight growing up, or unpredictable, or tied to someone else's mood. Watching the numbers closely was the sensible thing to do. The problem is that the strategy didn't get the memo that the situation changed.

So you keep watching. You feel guilty spending money you have. You find it hard to enjoy a holiday you can afford. You quietly resent people who seem relaxed about money, and you quietly worry you'll become them if you stop paying attention.

Joel went through a version of this himself. He had a tax return tab open on his laptop for six weeks. He knew roughly what it would say. He couldn't bring himself to click it. That's not avoidance in the classic sense — it's the vigilant person's version, where you stay close enough to feel in control but not close enough to feel the thing you're actually afraid of.

The work underneath this pattern isn't about checking less. It's about understanding what the checking is protecting you from. That's a different question than most money advice asks.

If this sounds like you, the [Money Script Quiz](/quiz) takes about four minutes and will tell you which pattern is running your financial decisions. It won't fix anything on its own. But it will name the thing you've been circling.

---
*Joel Berry, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner. Way of Wealth helps ambitious earners in their 20s and 30s understand the thinking behind their money decisions.*
